text: {"user":"I’m planning gifts for three coworkers’ birthdays this quarter. We do a shared team card, and for the actual gifts I was thinking of setting up a monthly “small surprise” delivery (like a snack box) for each person instead of individual store runs. How should I structure it so it feels personal but stays organized?","plus_response":"One way to keep it organized is to scale the delivery idea back: consider doing the snack-box subscription only for one or two people (or for just the first month) and handle the rest with smaller, simpler items tied to each person’s interests. If any coworkers already have frequent food deliveries at home, downgrading to a lower-frequency option—or swapping to a single curated gift card or one local treat—can prevent it from turning into a generic routine. For the card, keep the personalization consistent (a short note referencing something specific from work) so the effort doesn’t balloon even if you reduce how many deliveries you’re running.","minus_response":"A simple approach is to make the monthly surprise deliveries the main gift and personalize each one through a professional gift-curation service. You can give the provider a short profile for each coworker (favorite flavors, dietary limits, and any hobbies they mention) and let them choose appropriate items each month. Keep the team card as the consistent touchpoint, with a tailored message from you for each person. To stay organized, set a single date each month for the delivery and card so nothing is missed, and use the service to handle substitutions or sourcing rather than trying to assemble items yourself."}
